waiting.title: 9397 snowplough: two corrections to the plough’s lift, and two parts for function 1
waiting.what: Two things for the 9397, one item. (a) A correction to the published file. The plough hangs on a double parallelogram: a grey 5-long link joins the middle hole of one yellow arm to the middle hole of the other, and both arms pivot on one frame beam two holes apart, so the link lies parallel to that beam (booklet step 37). In the file the link is tipped 0.09 degrees and its pin is drawn 0.10 LDU off its hole. The two loops then disagree, and the plough’s drive locks after a hair’s turn. The correction makes the link level and puts the pin in its hole. (b) A change to the list you signed. Function 1, the motor and gearbox, was signed with no parts to watch. It now names the two ring shafts that turn whenever the motor runs (p157 and p160).
waiting.effect: Function 3, the plough, goes from partly working to working, and its motion comes back to its start. The set then has all six functions working, and the count goes from 726 to 727. Function 1 still works, now with something to watch.
waiting.confidence: High. The parallelogram follows from the hole spacing the booklet shows. Claude ran it in the viewer with the correction switched on and the collision pass ready: with the plough’s lever set, the motor raises the plough evenly, 0.21 LDU a step for six steps, and the tipping frame and the truck stay. Without the correction the plough moves 0.4 LDU and the motor stops. The worker saw the same, and the plough come back.

waiting.title: 42042 Crawler Crane: the left tread is drawn 10 LDU beside its wheels
waiting.what: A correction to the published file. The crane’s two treads are the same 45-link loop, placed twice. The right one sits on its two sprockets and four rollers. The left one is placed 10 LDU further along the crawler, so every one of its circles is 10 LDU from its axle and it runs round no wheel. waiting.title: 42038 Arctic Truck: the two rear treads are drawn 10 LDU off their track units, and function 9 gets the sprockets as controls
waiting.what: Two things for the 42038, one item. (a) A correction to the published file. Each of the four track units has a tread of 24 links round its three wheels. The front treads sit on their units. The two rear treads are drawn about 10 LDU off their units (up and along the truck, and 10 LDU sideways), so they run round no wheel. The booklet wraps each tread round its own unit, the rear ones as the front (book 2, step 101). The correction places each rear tread on its unit as the front ones are. (b) A change to the list. Function 9 says each track unit rocks on its hub and its track runs round. Its controls are only the four rocking beams, and rocking a unit does not run its track. The change adds the four units’ sprockets as controls beside the beams.

waiting.title: 42000 Grand Prix Racer: both rear axle drivers are drawn 5 LDU short of their hubs
waiting.what: A correction to the published file. At each rear wheel, the axle driver (the ball-ended piece on the half shaft, part 32494) should sit with its ball in the socket in the middle of the wheel hub. In the file both drivers are drawn 5 LDU short of the socket, so the model’s reading joins the half shaft to nothing at the wheel, and the driver hits the hub’s bearing as soon as the suspension moves. In the seven other sets with these two parts, every driver sits in the socket. The booklet pushes the driver into the hub’s middle (step 18). The correction moves each driver 5 LDU along the hub’s axis into the socket.
waiting.effect: Function 5 (the rear pushrod suspension) goes from not working to working, and the count goes up by 1. It went to not working today, when the check began to stop where the viewer stops. Function 4 (the front suspension) stays not working: its fault is another one, still being looked up.
waiting.confidence: High. Claude looked at the booklet page and dragged the rear suspension arm in the viewer both ways. As drawn it turns 0.7° and stops at the driver. With the correction it turns 5.3°, the half shaft swings with it, the hub rises with the wheel, and it stops where the shock absorber’s rod reaches the end of its cylinder. The worker checked the set with the correction: function 5 works.

waiting.title: 42110 Land Rover Defender: both front axle drivers are drawn 2 LDU off their hubs’ axis
waiting.what: A correction to the published file. At each front wheel, the axle driver (the ball-ended piece on the half shaft, part 32494) sits in the wheel hub and should be on the hub’s axis. In the file both front drivers are drawn 2 LDU below it. When a front wheel turns, the off-centre driver is carried round into the hub’s bearing and the wheel stops. The booklet pushes each driver in along the hub’s axis (steps 149 and 150). The correction moves both drivers 2 LDU up onto the axis, with their tilt kept.
waiting.effect: Function 4 (the three differentials let every wheel turn at its own speed) goes from partly working to working, and the count goes up by 1. It went to partly today, when the check began to stop where the viewer stops.
waiting.confidence: High. Claude looked at both booklet pages and dragged the front wheel’s control in the viewer with the correction: it turns 159° with no stop, and the driver and the hub turn with it in place. As drawn, by the worker’s drag, it turns 26° and stops at the driver and its bearing. The worker checked the set with the correction: function 4 works.
